item.title: Avalanche in Nepal leaves 2 dead, several missing
item.description: An avalanche has struck the Himlung Himal base camp in Nepal after days of severe weather. Two guides are confirmed dead and at least 14 people remain missing in the remote region.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: European cities seek ways of boosting affordable housing
item.description: In many major urban centers of Europe, the housing shortage has become an explosive social issue. DW looks into various models that have been put in place across the continent.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Iran sticks to Hormuz plan after Trump rejects it
item.description: Iranian officials that while they were aware of Trump's comments on rejecting the new proposal, they had not received a formal message rejecting the plan that would open the Strait of Hormuz.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: No public mentions of Taiwan at official Xi and Trump meeting
item.description: At a high-profile summit between Presidents Donald Trump and Xi Jinping in Washington, there was much talk of trade and artificial intelligence. One of the most contentious issues, Taiwan, was only discussed in private.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Powerful storm batters northeast US, hundreds of flights canceled
item.description: Hundreds of flights were canceled and thousands were delayed as a nor'easter brought flooding, power cuts and travel disruption to cities like New York, Boston and Philadelphia.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Backlash over data centers tests Europe's AI ambitions
item.description: Massive data centers needed to run AI are triggering protests across Europe. Their operators counter that they boost digital sovereignty and energy independence.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Russia expected to intensify hybrid war on Europe
item.description: Drone explosions, airspace violations, arson attacks: Poland, Romania, and Moldova are now regularly targeted in Russian attacks against Ukraine. More governments are calling these attacks deliberate acts of aggression.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Pakistan: Suicide attack at police stop kills at least 11
item.description: The blast was claimed by the Pakistani Taliban, which has stepped up attacks on Pakistani security forces in recent years.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Russian students: Propaganda in school prepares them to die
item.description: The Russian government wants children to learn about patriotism from an early age. DW spoke to students in Siberia about their views on propaganda at school on the war in Ukraine and their future.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: South Korea's gender pay gap grows as women get older
item.description: A new report shows how in South Korea, women on average earn less and have fewer employment opportunities throughout their lives.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Lula or Bolsonaro as president? Brazil gears up to vote
item.description: Brazilians go to the polls on October 4. The front-runners are multilateralist incumbent Lula da Silva and former President Jair Bolsonaro's son, Flavio, who wants to bring Brazil closer to the US and away from China.
